correctness.rationale: At fixed positive squared spectrum, the signed difference is a rational function with common denominator of degree q and numerator degree at most q-1; identical score curves are separated from nontrivial differences. The prescribed root polynomial is realized via explicit residues, alternating signs, disjoint-support first-two singular-vector rows, and an exact positive square-root orthonormal completion. The construction works for every q>=2, every distinct positive squared singular spectrum and every increasing set of q-1 positive roots. The example is checked symbolically, and the embedded script passed 540 checks on exact partial fractions and independently computed full-matrix resolvents; these finite checks are not a universal proof.

originality.rationale: The fully specified McCurdy 2018 ridge-score sorting rule, Meier–Nakatsukasa 2022 multi-parameter regularized least-squares algorithms, and Cohen–Musco–Musco ridge-score sampling literature were inspected for corresponding implications. Their statements are about sampling/spectral preservation or preconditioning, not a universal sharp positive-parameter crossing count and full prescribed-location realization satisfying orthonormal singular-vector constraints. published-finding corpus searches for direct terminology and rational-transform aliases did not return equivalent quantitative claims. Classical rational-function/interpolation priority remains a material residual risk; the failed searches are not treated as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: An uninspected matrix analysis or total-positivity/Stieltjes-transform literature source may already state a theoretically equivalent sharp construction; independent priority review has not occurred.
No claim about broad sorting-path complexity or algorithmic performance is inferred from the pairwise result.

value.rationale: Ridge leverage scores are directly used to sort column importance in deterministic sampling (McCurdy 2018) and regularization parameters are varied in numerical least squares (Meier–Nakatsukasa 2022). The theorem answers a natural missing ranking-path question exactly: despite individual monotonicity, two sampling priorities can reverse the maximum rank-controlled number of times at any assigned positive parameter values. The construction respects all common-matrix SVD constraints, an essential step beyond a formal polynomial degree observation. It supplies a structural limitation on reusing ranked importance over a parameter path; it does not assert an algorithmic runtime or approximation-error improvement.
